skill.name: cold-email
skill.description: Write B2B cold emails and follow-up sequences that get replies. Use when the user wants to write cold outreach emails, prospecting emails, cold email campaigns, sales development emails, or SDR emails. Also use when the user mentions "cold outreach," "prospecting email," "outbound email," "email to leads," "reach out to prospects," "sales email," "follow-up email sequence," "nobody's replying to my emails," or "how do I write a cold email." Covers subject lines, opening lines, body copy, CTAs, personalization, and multi-touch follow-up sequences. For warm/lifecycle email sequences, see emails. For sales collateral beyond emails, see sales-enablement.
skill.summary: Create concise, personalized B2B cold emails and follow-up sequences with clear, low-friction calls to action.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

semantic_findings.title: Deceptive Outreach Framing
semantic_findings.description: The guidance recommends subject lines that resemble internal colleague messages so recipients do not classify them as vendor outreach. This can enable deceptive social-engineering-style contact.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited section explicitly calls the tactic internal camouflage and says it should look like colleague email. The deceptive framing is direct and unambiguous.

content.user_title: Write B2B Cold Emails That Earn Replies
content.value_statement: Generic outreach is ignored because it lacks relevance and a clear reason to reply. This skill creates concise, personalized B2B emails and follow-up sequences with focused calls to action.
actual_capabilities: Drafts first-touch B2B emails from recipient, offer, research signal, proof, and desired outcome.
Creates three-to-five-email follow-up sequences that introduce a new angle or value point at each touch.
Generates concise subject lines tailored to audience context and the email topic.
Adjusts voice, detail, and call-to-action friction for executives, managers, and technical recipients.
Reviews and rewrites outreach for relevance, brevity, credibility, personalization, and one clear ask.
limitations: Does not verify prospect facts, email addresses, legal compliance, or cited benchmark sources.
Does not send, schedule, track, or measure email campaigns.
Output quality depends on accurate recipient context, a specific value proposition, and truthful proof.
Focuses on B2B cold outreach, not lifecycle, support, newsletter, or transactional email.

use_cases.title: Launch Founder Outreach
use_cases.description: Turn a clear offer and prospect signal into a short founder-led email with a credible reason to reply.

use_cases.title: Build SDR Sequences
use_cases.description: Create a coordinated first touch and follow-ups that rotate proof, insights, and useful resources.

use_cases.title: Improve Campaign Copy
use_cases.description: Review existing outreach and rewrite weak openings, vague claims, crowded messages, and high-friction calls to action.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a First Email
prompt_templates.prompt: Write one B2B cold email to [role] at [company]. We offer [solution] for [problem]. Use [proof] and ask for [desired response].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the offer and recipient are known but no draft exists.

prompt_templates.title: Connect a Research Signal
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a personalized cold email for [recipient]. Connect [verified signal] to [relevant problem] without exaggeration. Keep one proof point and one low-friction question.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a verified company or person signal should support the opening.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Follow-Up Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a four-email sequence for [audience] promoting [offer]. Rotate these angles: [insight], [proof], and [resource]. End with a respectful final message.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when planning a complete outreach sequence with distinct value in every message.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Rewrite a Campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the campaign below for relevance, clarity, credibility, and pressure. Identify weak claims and disconnected personalization. Rewrite every message for [audience]. Provide three subject options and explain the strongest choice.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced optimization of an existing multi-message campaign.

output_examples.input: Write to a vice president of sales who is hiring four SDRs. Offer a coaching workflow and ask whether an example would help.
output_examples.output:
Subject: SDR ramp

Jordan,

Hiring four SDRs usually creates a coaching bottleneck for sales leaders. Our workflow gives managers one review queue for calls and follow-ups.

Would a brief example be useful?

Morgan

output_examples.input: Write the first follow-up for the SDR coaching email. Add a new resource instead of repeating the original message.
output_examples.output:
Subject: SDR ramp

Jordan,

One additional thought: new representatives often build separate processes during onboarding. I can send a checklist for standardizing call and follow-up reviews.

Worth sending?

Morgan

best_practices: Use only verified recipient and company details, then connect each detail to the problem the offer addresses.
Keep each message concise, include one proof point, and end with one low-friction call to action.
Add fresh value in every follow-up and stop after the stated final message or any opt-out.
anti_patterns: Do not invent research signals, customer results, urgency, mutual connections, or familiarity.
Do not hide commercial intent with false reply prefixes, misleading sender identity, or colleague impersonation.
Do not send generic templates, feature lists, multiple links, or repeated follow-ups that add no value.

faq.question: What information produces the strongest draft?
faq.answer: Provide the recipient role, company, verified trigger, relevant problem, offer, proof, and desired response.

faq.question: Can this skill research prospects?
faq.answer: It can use supplied context and available product marketing files. It does not independently verify prospect facts or data sources.

faq.question: How long should a sequence be?
faq.answer: The guidance recommends three to five total emails with increasing gaps and a distinct value point in every follow-up.

faq.question: Can it send or track emails?
faq.answer: No. It writes and reviews copy but does not send, schedule, monitor, or measure campaigns.

faq.question: How does it personalize messages?
faq.answer: It connects a verified person, role, company, or market signal to the specific problem addressed by the offer.

faq.question: Does it guarantee legal compliance or replies?
faq.answer: No. Users must follow applicable outreach laws, honor preferences and opt-outs, verify claims, and assess campaign performance.
